A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MMD Guidance research. Text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-C are readable, and retained content can be matched across layout changes and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian-mixture simulations and image-generation experiments, including quantitative comparisons, sensitivity analyses, and qualitative outputs in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds domain-gap tests, component ablations, larger-reference comparisons, and late-step guidance experiments.

M1.justification: The MMD objective, sampling updates, latent encoding, product-kernel conditioning, and Algorithms 1-2 remain unchanged. Restricting guidance to the final 30 steps is evaluated as a schedule ablation of the existing method.

E1.justification: v2 adds synthetic GMM scenarios with widely separated clusters and shifted target centers (Table 5 and Figure 16). Existing image datasets, conditional-generation tasks, and painting-style adaptation remain covered; the painting experiment already appeared in v1.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in retained experiments are unchanged. Domain Guidance already appears in v1 Table 1, despite receiving a new discussion paragraph in v2. The larger-reference GMM experiment reuses the existing fine-tuning and unguided comparators.

E3.justification: Existing benchmark settings largely persist, but v2 adds substantial experimental designs: component-removal controls, 3,000-point GMM reference sets, and final-30-step versus full guidance. It also describes gradient-error evaluation against a 10,000-reference approximation, averaged over 1,000 generated samples. These are added protocols, not established reruns of the original comparisons.

E4.justification: v2 adds diversity-term ablations on GMMs and FFHQ (Tables 18-19), domain-gap robustness tests, larger-reference fine-tuning comparisons, and late-step guidance analysis with generation trajectories. These substantially expand investigation of component necessity, applicability, and guidance timing beyond v1's retained kernel, reference-size, and noisy-reference analyses.

E5.justification: v2 removes uncertainty entries from main Table 1. Appendix Table 7 preserves them for MMD, user-trained models, and fine-tuning, but not the FFHQ unguided, CG, or Domain Guidance rows. Both versions retain the five-seed averaging statement and uncertainty reporting in other benchmark tables.

E6.justification: Tables 5, 16, 18-20, and 22 add substantial quantitative evidence. For example, Table 19 newly reports sunglasses FD of 941.49 with the cross term alone versus 692.87 with full MMD; Table 22 adds late-step FD of 1732.23. Most earlier benchmark results persist, while selected RRKE entries, runtime sample-count entries, and qualitative examples are removed.

T1.justification: The pointwise, uniform, and product-kernel concentration results, assumptions, and Appendix A proofs are retained under new numbering. The omitted Gaussian-specific MMD-gradient display specializes the retained general gradient; its underlying Gaussian derivative remains in Appendix A.2.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: training-free distribution matching through MMD gradients, prompt-aware product kernels, and efficient latent-space implementation. The additional experiments support these claims without materially redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations that larger domain gaps require stronger guidance and more references, later denoising stages are especially important, and MMD remains competitive when fine-tuning has sufficient data. Existing sparse-reference and kernel-choice limitations remain; the new Impact Statement also discusses dependence on reference-data biases.

D1.justification: The v2 abstract newly provides a project-code repository link. Added experiments disclose reference counts and guidance intervals, while existing implementation information, including kernel choices, guidance-scale ranges, encoders, and timing hardware, is largely retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially broadens related-work coverage with RKE/Vendi-based diversity guidance and kernel-based online model selection, embedding alignment, and generative-model comparison. This expands the research context beyond the retained discussion of adaptation and MMD training losses, rather than merely updating citation formatting.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the section sequence remain recognizable. Changes include the title prefix, shortened explanations and headings, additional experimental discussion, and new Acknowledgments and Impact Statement sections. The conclusion is relabeled to explicitly mention limitations.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main layout, extensively repositions and resizes displays, and condenses Tables 1-3. It adds ablation, domain-gap, and trajectory displays while removing v1's bike, car, and painting galleries (Figures 12, 13, and 17). These are substantial presentation changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: The added component ablations and larger-reference fine-tuning comparison strengthen validation of the existing method, while Table 16 supplies quantitative support missing from v1's painting experiment. The code link improves access information. The net gain is tempered by lost FFHQ baseline uncertainty and a new gradient-accuracy claim without a corresponding error table or plot.
